ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the circuit in the attached figure, a voltage v(t) is applied between terminals a-b, with terminal a labeled positive and terminal b labeled negative. The input current i(t) flows in from terminal a to the right, first passing through a series inductor L; the node at the right end of the inductor is then connected to a parallel branch, which is composed of a 100 μF capacitor and a 100 Ω resistor, and the lower ends of both are connected back to terminal b. Therefore, the impedance looking into a-b is the series inductor impedance plus the parallel impedance of the 100 Ω resistor and the 100 μF capacitor. Reasoning calculation: Given angular frequency ω = 100 rad/s, the capacitor impedance Z_C = 1/(jωC) = 1/(j × 100 × 100×10^-6) = 1/(j0.01) = -j100 Ω. The parallel branch impedance Z_p = 100 || (-j100) = (100 × -j100)/(100 - j100) = 50 - j50 Ω. The total input impedance Z = jωL + Z_p = jωL + 50 - j50 = 50 + j(ωL - 50). The problem states that the inductor current i(t) and the terminal voltage v(t) are in phase; this means the input current and input voltage are in phase, so the total impedance must be purely real, i.e. Im(Z)=0. Thus ωL - 50 = 0, that is, ωL = 50. At this time Z = 50 Ω, purely real, so |Z| = 50 Ω.

method.method_draft: First describe the image: current enters terminal a, passes through the inductor L, then splits into a parallel 100 Ω resistor and 100 μF capacitor connected to terminal b. Take the input/inductor current I as the phasor reference, as required by the text condition that I and v(t) become in phase. At ω = 100 rad/s, the capacitor reactance magnitude is 100 Ω, so the shunt branch R || C has an equivalent drop per ampere with components 50 Ω in phase with I and -50 Ω in quadrature, i.e. Z_p = 50 - j50 Ω. The series inductor contributes only a +jX_L quadrature drop. The phase condition means the -50 Ω capacitive quadrature component of the shunt branch must be exactly cancelled by +X_L from the inductor. After this cancellation, only the 50 Ω in-phase component remains, so the input impedance magnitude is 50 Ω.
